findings.head: 34121cc7874a
findings.finding: TestContainerPID's failure cases run containerPID with a 300 ms wall-clock limit, and two of their outcomes depend on the runner spawning the fake runtime fast enough: 'listed, no process' requires listed to be recorded, i.e. two runs of the shell script (plus the 20 ms poll) to complete inside 300 ms; 'run exited' requires the in.done branch of the select, but if the first inspect takes over 300 ms both in.done and ctx.Done are ready and select picks either, giving the timeout message. That is wall-clock on the success path of an assertion, which TEST-04 forbids and which the design's Validation plan rules out ('wall-clock used only as a failure bound'). It passed 100/100 here under 4-core CPU load, so the margin is wide, but this item exists to remove a timing-dependent outcome.
findings.fix: Make the outcome follow the fake's call count, not the clock: give every case a one-minute limit; for 'run exited' that alone makes it deterministic (in.done is closed before the call); for the two timeout cases pass a parent context the test cancels once the fake's count file reaches the number of answers (or have the fake write a marker the test waits on), and assert the message without the limit's value or with the one-minute value.

fixed_at.head: 4d95ad85552e
fixed_at.commit: 4d95ad8 launch: time out TestContainerPID's failure cases by the fake's calls

findings.resolution: Judged fixed. Every case now runs containerPID with a one-minute limit (relay_test.go:265). 'run exited' closes in.done before the call, so the first poll's select takes in.done unless one inspect outlasts the minute: a failure bound only. The two timeout cases cancel a parent context from cancelPastAnswers (relay_test.go:297) once the fake's count file exceeds the number of answers; the fake increments the count before it answers and containerPID inspects one call at a time, so count > n means the n-th answer was read and listed recorded, whatever the speed. After the cancel each path (inspect killed, or the StartPoll wait) reaches ctx.Done with in.done open, so the message is the timeout one, its text fixed by the limit argument (1m0s), not by elapsed time. The fired check after the call fails the case only if containerPID returned before the fake gave every answer, which only the one-minute bound can cause. close(fired) precedes cancel(), so the check is race-free. The 1 ms poll paces the watcher and decides no outcome. No wall-clock is left in what an assertion checks; the phase-order check compares monotonic readings of sequential code. 300/300 under -race here with concurrent load; Implement's 1200/1200 under CPU load.
